source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines graph parents by structural parent sets and bidirected edges by shared exogenous variables, gives S-ID from P(V|S=1), presents a sound Algorithm 1, states its completeness as a conjecture, and gives the displayed selected functional as Eq. (23).

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3–4, Definition 7 and Theorem 4; p. 7, positive binary countermodel construction
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves ordinary semi-Markovian hedge nonidentifiability, with C-forest hedge witnesses and binary countermodels sharing P(V); it does not address normalized selected-law equality.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 4, Lemma 17; pp. 4–5, intervention caveat and Example 21; p. 13, Proposition 22
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper introduces a forward conditioning operation, proves commutation with interventions only outside selection ancestors and with marginalization, and explicitly shows general noncommutation for ancestor interventions.

The paper proves completeness for conditional generalized identification from specified mixtures of observational/interventional Q[S] distributions under positivity; this is not identification from one selected law P(V|S=1).

The paper studies graphical identification from data collected under different experimental conditions with systematic selection and provides a general identification algorithm, i.e. a distinct multi-regime data-fusion input from the proposal's single selected-law problem.

The application uses nonoverlapping UK Biobank gene-exposure and gene-outcome samples and a two-sample MR analysis, making the proposed two-selector audit a conditional diagnostic rather than a claim that the publication already established its exact-graph feasibility result.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Solve and publish the exact rational certificate for the two-virtual-edge base graph, including its full tables and checker transcript, before attempting the universal lift.
Make the contingent chain-incidence completeness pivot a stated boundary theorem: define the incidence class and prove its inclusion in the published augmented-ADMG class.
Add a worked two-selector UK Biobank graph and state exactly which raw individual-level margins, covariates, and selector information would be required to instantiate the audit.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 on the compositional inverse-lift kernel, with the two-virtual-edge rational fiber computation as the first kill test.
